title: Small-divisor completion gives a rig-regular locally principal formal variety
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-exc-excellent-ring], and let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor: its ideal $I$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. Suppose $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq |D|$, where $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ is the set of nonregular points [def-weil-regular-scheme], and suppose $D$ is a finite disjoint union of finite-type schemes over characteristic-zero fields [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $\mathfrak X=\widehat X_D$, formed on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ by $\operatorname{Spf}(\varprojlim_n B/I^n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\mathfrak I=I\mathcal O_{\mathfrak X}$. A Noetherian scheme means one with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. A Noetherian adic formal scheme is a ringed space admitting a finite open cover by spaces of the form $\operatorname{Spf}B$, the space of open prime ideals of a Noetherian ring $B$ complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal, with its completed structure sheaf. Such a formal scheme is reduced when its affine chart rings are reduced. Quasi-excellence means quasi-excellence of its affine chart rings [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Regularity of a formal scheme means regularity of the rings on its formal affine charts [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its singular locus is defined on $\operatorname{Spf}B$ by the radical ideal of the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Then $\mathfrak X$ is reduced, Noetherian and quasi-excellent. The ideal $\mathfrak I$ is an invertible ideal of definition, and $\mathfrak X$ is a finite disjoint union of formal varieties of characteristic zero: each reduced closed fibre is of finite type over a characteristic-zero field. Its singular locus is the formal completion of the reduced closed subscheme $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ along $D$ and is defined by an open ideal. In particular it is rig-regular, meaning that locally some power of the ideal of definition is contained in the ideal defining its singular locus. The empty divisor gives the empty formal scheme.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.4.1, printed p.26, citing [Tem1, 3.1.5(ii)]; §§2.4.1,2.4.3,2.4.9,2.4.11 and 3.1.1--3.1.4; Theorem 2.1.6. No Stacks tag states this combined formal-geometric input. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover of $X$. Each affine spectrum is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], so the local Cartier trivializations admit a finite affine refinement. Write a member as $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $I|_U=(t)$ and multiplication by $t$ injective on $B$. Put $A=\varprojlim_n B/I^n$ and $K=IA$. Since $B$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $A$ is Noetherian, $K$-adically complete and $A/K\cong B/I$, compatibly with the quotient maps. Thus the formal affine charts in the definition of $\widehat X_D$ are Noetherian, have ideal of definition $K$, and have closed fibre $D\cap U$. These charts give a finite cover because the chosen affine cover of $X$ is finite.

source.place: Tags 0316, lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian, and 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated; Temkin §2.4.1 for the formal charts

proof.text: The quotient $B/I$ is quasi-excellent: it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian], a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] because $B\to B/I$ is of finite type (generated by the empty list) and $B$ is a G-ring, and J-2 because every finite type $B/I$-algebra is a finite type $B$-algebra, so the J-2 condition of $B$ in [def-exc-excellent-ring] applies to it. The ring $A$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra, and Step 1 gives its Noetherianity, completeness and quotient $A/K\cong B/I$. Apply [lem-per-qe-complete-pair-lifting] with $(A,K)$ to obtain quasi-excellence of $A$. This also applies to every formal distinguished open: its ring is the completion of $A_f$ along $KA_f$. The ring $A_f\cong A[x]/(fx-1)$ is quasi-excellent by the same three checks: Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring], and J-2 since finite type $A_f$-algebras are finite type $A$-algebras. Step 1 and complete-pair lifting then apply to $(A_f,KA_f)$. Hence the formal scheme is quasi-excellent, in the chartwise sense of the statement.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.6 and §§2.4.1, 2.4.3; Stacks more-algebra.tex Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, and the J-2 definition (label definition-J) for the quotient/localization input

proof.text: Quasi-excellence of $B$ includes the G-ring condition [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular] makes $B\to A$ regular. Since $B$ is reduced and both rings are Noetherian, [lem-exc-regular-map-reduced-target] implies that $A$ is reduced. For the Cartier ideal, use flatness of $B\to A$ and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] on $0\to B\xrightarrow{t}B$. Its tensor is $0\to A\xrightarrow{t}A$, so $t$ stays a non-zero-divisor and $A\xrightarrow{t}tA=K$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. The local identifications exhibit the extended ideal $\mathfrak I$ as invertible; its powers define the formal topology by Step 1. This proves both reducedness and local principality without assuming the divisor is reduced.

source.place: Tags 0AH2, lemma-map-G-ring-to-completion-regular, and 07QK, lemma-reduced-goes-up; flat tensor exactness as in algebra.tex Tag 00HB

proof.text: We check regular loci point by point, so that the singular-locus assertion is an argument rather than an assumed compatibility. For $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] the local rings are Noetherian, and by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] the local map $B_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular. Its flatness and regular closed fibre, together with [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre], imply that regularity of $B_{\mathfrak p}$ implies regularity of $A_{\mathfrak q}$. Conversely, flatness and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] imply that regularity of $A_{\mathfrak q}$ implies regularity of $B_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is exactly the inverse image of that of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. This argument works for any regular map between Noetherian rings, including the chart-restriction maps used below.

source.place: §2.1.10, compatibility with regular morphisms, and §2.4.9; Stacks Tags 07C0, 031E and 00OF

proof.text: Let $J\subseteq B$ be the radical ideal of the nonregular locus; this locus is closed by the J-2 condition in [def-exc-excellent-ring], applied to the identity finite-type algebra. The map $B/J\to A/JA$ is the base change of the regular map $B\to A$ along the finite-type quotient $B\to B/J$, so it is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change]. Both quotient rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian], and $B/J$ is reduced. Hence [lem-exc-regular-map-reduced-target] implies that $A/JA$ is reduced: $JA$ is radical. Step 4 says its zero set is the nonregular locus, so $JA$ is exactly the singular ideal of $A$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor], for the cyclic $B$-module $B/J$, identifies $A/JA\cong A\otimes_B(B/J)\cong\varprojlim_n B/(J+I^n)$. The maps are $a\otimes\bar b\mapsto a b\bmod JA$ and $a\otimes\bar b\mapsto(a_n b\bmod(J+I^n))_n$; these formulas preserve products and the quotient maps. Thus the closed formal subscheme defined by $JA$ is precisely the completion of $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ along $I$.

source.place: §2.4.9; Stacks Tags 07C1, lemma-regular-base-change, 07QK, lemma-reduced-goes-up, and 00MA, lemma-completion-tensor

proof.text: The preceding identifications glue as ideals, not merely as closed point sets. Indeed a formal distinguished restriction of $\operatorname{Spf}A$ has ring $C=\widehat{A_f}_{KA_f}$. The ring $A_f$ is quasi-excellent by Step 2 ([lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring], [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring]); $A\to A_f$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular], and $A_f\to C$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular]. Their composite is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition]; its fibre rings are Noetherian since $C$ is Noetherian by Step 1 and localizations and quotients preserve Noetherianity ([lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]). Applying Steps 4--5 to $A\to C$ shows that the extension of the singular ideal $JA$ is exactly the singular ideal of $C$. Consequently the affine ideals and the completion isomorphisms agree on a basis of each overlap. They therefore define the global singular formal subscheme and identify it with $\widehat{X_{\mathrm{sing}}}_D$.

source.place: §§2.4.1,2.4.3,2.4.9; formal localizations are regular; Stacks Tags 0AH2 and 07QI, lemma-regular-composition

proof.text: The inclusion $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq |D|$ says $V(J)\subseteq V(I)$ on each $U$, hence $I\subseteq\sqrt J=J$. In fact the weaker radical inclusion suffices: [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] gives $I^N\subseteq J$ for some $N\geq1$, and extending ideals gives $K^N\subseteq JA$. Therefore the singular ideal on every completed chart is open. This is exactly rig-regularity as defined in the statement. We use containment of ideals, rather than the unsupported implication that an arbitrary formal subscheme with closed-point support on the closed fibre has an open ideal.

By Step 1 the closed fibre defined by $\mathfrak I$ is $D$, so the reduced closed fibre is $D_{\mathrm{red}}$. Write $D=\coprod_{i=1}^rD_i$ with $D_i$ finite type over a characteristic-zero field $k_i$. The underlying topological space of the completion is $|D|$; its clopen partition by the $|D_i|$ therefore gives a finite disjoint union of open and closed formal subschemes. The reduced closed fibre of the $i$th is $(D_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$, which is finite type over $k_i$: on a finite affine cover of $D_i$, pass from a finitely generated $k_i$-algebra to its quotient by the nilradical, keeping the same generators. Thus each piece is a formal variety in precisely the sense defined in the statement. If $D=\varnothing$, then $I=B$ on every affine chart and every quotient $B/I^n$ is zero; the completion is the empty formal scheme. These arguments also cover $X=\varnothing$.

lean.statement: theorem SmallSingularLocusPair.formalCompletion_geometry (P : SmallSingularLocusPair.{u}) : AdicFormalCompletion.IsNoetherianFormalSpace P.completion.space ∧ P.completion.IsReducedQuasiExcellent ∧ (∀ U : P.scheme.affineOpens, Nonempty (P.completion.chartSpace U ≅ AdicFormalCompletion.formalSpectrum (.of (P.completion.chartRing U)) (P.completion.chartIdeal U))) ∧ Nonempty (P.completion.space ≃ₜ P.completion.closedFibre) ∧ P.completion.HasInvertibleIdealOfDefinition ∧ P.completion.IsFiniteDisjointUnionOfFormalVarieties ∧ P.completion.HasCompletedSingularLocus ∧ P.completion.IsRigRegular ∧ (P.divisor = ⊤ → IsEmpty P.completion.space)
